Define an Effect for sim_model()

Source: R/sim-model.R
sim_effect.Rd

For each term of from, adds coef * term to the linear predictor of to: its log-hazard if to is a sim_process(), or the lp passed to its draw if it's a sim_mark().

Usage

sim_effect(formula, coef)

Arguments

formula

to ~ from, with to the affected process or mark. from is one or more terms separated by +; wrap a sum in parentheses to make it one term. A term is an R expression of covariates (their value) and processes (their number of events so far), which may also use:

t

The current time (see sim_events()'s time_step).

event_time()

Time of a process's k-th or k-th latest event.

<name>(s)

The value of covariate, mark or process count name at time s, after any update at s, e.g. bp(event_time(operation, 1)).

coef

Numeric vector, one coefficient per term of from.

Value

A sim_effect, for sim_model()'s effects.

See also

sim_model(), event_time()

Examples

sim_effect(death ~ age, coef = 0.03)
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.03 * age
sim_effect(death ~ age + relapse, coef = c(0.03, 1))
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.03 * age + 1 * relapse
sim_effect(death ~ (age + bmi), coef = 0.02)
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.02 * (age + bmi)
sim_effect(death ~ (age - 60)^2 + (relapse == 3), coef = c(0.001, 1.2))
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.001 * ((age - 60)^2) + 1.2 * (relapse == 3)
sim_effect(death ~ checkup > 0 & t - event_time(checkup, -1) < 1, coef = 0.5)
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.5 * (checkup > 0 & t - event_time(checkup, -1) < 1)
sim_effect(death ~ operation * bp(event_time(operation, 1)), coef = 0.02)
#> <sim_effect> death ~ 0.02 * (operation * bp(event_time(operation, 1)))
